purpose.summary: Current-state host platform contract for modules integrating into BI Core Shell.
goals: Declare currently supported Core Shell capabilities.
Give module owners a practical integration boundary.
Reduce direct coupling to legacy src/core compatibility code.
Make module manifests and host capabilities understandable as two sides of the same integration contract.

notes: Core Shell is the target platform layer for new shared/platform capabilities.
Runtime/orchestration is still partially hybrid because src/core/runtime.js remains active.
This manifest describes currently usable host capabilities and boundaries, not a target-state redesign.

available.summary: Official access path for allowed ERP batch fetches.
ERP DSN resolution and ERP credential/config access path.
SMS gateway outbox dir, SMS ledger root, and SMS contract defaults.
Public durable JSON write entry point and storage backend facade.
Module runtime registration and lookup by use_case.
PostgreSQL and DB platform config loading.
Node/XLSX workbook support checks and matrix extraction for EOJN-style analysis.

partial.summary: Runtime registration is partly in Core Shell but compatibility runtime entry remains in legacy core.
Shared durable JSON writes are normalized, but many module-specific artifact outputs remain specialized.
SMS config access is centralized, while ledger/outbox publish internals remain legacy.

intentionally_split.summary: Workbook ingest is not one unified host capability today and must not be merged casually.

not_generic_host_capabilities.summary: Public website/API fetches such as EOJN procurements/notices remain module-specific and are not declared as generic Core Shell fetch capabilities.

integration_rules: Use Core Shell ERP fetch capability instead of a module-local ERP client.
Use Core Shell config access paths for shared/platform config values.
Use Core Shell storage entry points for shared durable JSON writes.
Do not import src/core_shell/storage/fs_store.js directly outside storage internals.
Do not add new shared/platform code to src/core/*.
Do not assume workbook ingest is one unified service.
Do not expand src/api/server.js with module-specific orchestration if an existing runtime/module path can be used.

allowed_dependency_flow: api -> modules only through approved orchestration/runtime contract
core_shell must not import from modules

known_open_gaps: route-level orchestration is still heavy in src/api/server.js
artifact lifecycle is not normalized across all modules
logging and audit are not yet formalized as one Core Shell contract
SMS runtime/storage/publish internals remain partly legacy
some module-specific durable writes remain direct and specialized
